name: Costain Group PLC
executive_summary: Costain Group PLC is a UK infrastructure solutions specialist focused on transport, water, energy and defence, trading on modest multiples (P/E 16.5×, P/B 2.3×, yield 2.3%) despite a net-cash balance sheet and a record £7.0bn forward work position. FY2025 revenue fell to £1,045.7m as legacy road frameworks rolled off and HS2 was rescheduled, yet adjusted operating margin expanded to 4.5% and adjusted free cash flow reached £63.1m. H1 2026 interim results confirm profit growth, net cash of £164.4m, and unchanged full-year guidance, with management targeting a revenue and margin step-change from FY2027 as AMP8 water and grid investment ramp. The central debate is whether margin expansion and capital returns (doubled interim dividend, £20m buyback) justify the screen's buy signal while reported revenue has declined for four years and Transportation margins remain thin — or whether the order book and customer diversification into regulated utilities and aviation de-risk the cyclical construction narrative.
investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen rates Costain a **buy**: 13 of 22 models pass across five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk), composite score 70%, data quality 20/20, with passes on Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Lynch/Neff PEG variants, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Piotroski F-Score, Earnings Quality and Financial Health. Key screen metrics — P/E 16.5, P/B 2.3, yield 2.3%, ROE 15.2%, debt/equity ~13% — fit a post-turnaround contractor with improving earnings quality rather than a distressed cyclical.

Business quality has improved materially. Management's stated KPI — adjusted operating margin — rose from 3.0% (FY2023) to 3.4% (FY2024) to 4.5% (FY2025), exceeding the 4.5% run-rate target per the FY2025 annual report (Companies House extract). The contract portfolio is predominantly long-term target-cost frameworks with no single-stage lump-sum contracts at year-end FY2025. Forward work grew from £5.4bn (FY2024) to a record £7.0bn (FY2025), maintained through H1 2026, with customer mix shifting toward private and regulated clients (48% of forward work at H1 2026 vs 30% in FY2023).

Balance-sheet strength supports the value case: net cash £189.3m at FY2025 year-end (FY2024: £158.5m), undrawn £100m revolving credit facility extended to September 2030, and bonding facilities of £295m with utilisation of £71.2m at H1 2026. The January 2026 pension agreement removed dividend-parity constraints and eliminated scheduled deficit contributions through January 2031, with the scheme in a £62.9m IAS 19 surplus at 30 June 2026.

For a value investor, the hook is a cash-rich, improving-margin business on mid-teens earnings multiples, with visible multi-year revenue from regulated infrastructure cycles (AMP8 water ~£100bn industry capex; RIIO-3 grid upgrade) and a credible path to above 5% adjusted operating margins. The screen's neutral timing signal (RSI 62, price ~23% above 200-day MA, conviction 44% on a new one-week signal) suggests accumulation rather than urgency.
financial_review:
**Primary source:** Companies House annual extracts (FY2023–FY2025) and Investegate RNS (H1 2026 interim, 14 May 2026 AGM trading update). Yahoo `financials_annual.json` used only for cross-check; figures align with filings.

**Annual trend**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | £1,332.0m | £1,251.1m | £1,045.7m |
| Adjusted operating profit | £40.1m | £43.1m | £47.1m |
| Adjusted operating margin | 3.0% | 3.4% | 4.5% |
| Reported operating profit | — | £31.1m | £44.8m |
| Adjusted basic EPS | — | 14.6p | 14.5p |
| Adjusted free cash flow | — | £27.1m | £63.1m |
| Net cash (year-end) | — | £158.5m | £189.3m |
| Forward work | — | £5.4bn | £7.0bn |

*(FY2022 revenue £1,421.4m cited in FY2024 annual extract.)*

Revenue has declined for four consecutive years, driven by completion of low-margin Regional Delivery Partnership road projects, HS2 schedule revisions, and the AMP7-to-AMP8 water transition. Profitability has diverged positively: margin expansion and lower adjusting items (£2.3m in FY2025 vs £12.0m in FY2024) lifted reported operating profit 44% year-on-year despite a 16% revenue decline. Adjusted EPS was essentially flat at 14.5p as buybacks and operating gains were offset by a higher effective tax rate and lower net finance income. Yahoo reports FY2025 operating cash flow £51.3m and FCF £48.5m — consistent with filing adjusted FCF of £63.1m (Yahoo fallback for cross-check only).

**Interim and trading updates**

*H1 2026 (13 August 2026):* Revenue £543.1m (+3.4%); adjusted operating profit £17.3m (+3.0%), margin 3.2%; reported PBT £19.2m; basic EPS 5.7p; net cash £164.4m after £8.2m dividends and £7.6m buybacks; adjusted free cash outflow £1.4m (H2-weighted); interim dividend doubled to 2.0p; forward work maintained at £7.0bn (91% visibility of FY2026/FY2027 consensus revenues). Natural Resources +13.3% (Water +15.1%, Energy +25.7%; margin 6.9%); Transportation −3.2% (Road −32.6%; margin 2.5%).

*AGM trading update (14 May 2026):* Trading in line; FY2026 adjusted operating margin target ~4.0%; net cash expected ~£175m year-end.

**Gaps:** Only one interim RNS body in the index (H1 2026); prior interim bodies absent. Annual body extracts lack full audited statements and detailed risk/viability prose. Yahoo quarterly cash-flow series is empty (TTM cashflow suppressed).
risks_and_flags:
**Contract and programme execution.** HS2 remains material. FY2025 revenue was reduced by a revised schedule; H1 2026 notes the programme is navigating a change in delivery strategy with Skanska-Costain-Strabag JV discussions underway. Sector news on HS2 Old Oak Common cost overruns (6 August 2026) highlights industry-wide pressure.

**Revenue vs margin tension.** Four years of declining revenue despite margin gains. Transportation margins (2.5% H1 2026) lag Natural Resources (6.9%).

**Customer and regulatory concentration.** Forward work includes 29% central government; water/energy exposure carries Ofwat/Ofgem regulatory risk.

**Working capital and cash timing.** FY2026 net cash guidance (~£170–175m) assumes partial unwind of historic working capital benefits. H1 adjusted FCF was negative; H2 weighting introduces execution risk.

**Pension.** January 2026 agreement removed dividend parity and cash contributions through January 2031; scheme in £62.9m IAS 19 surplus at H1 2026. Longevity, inflation and investment risks remain; Virgin Media / NTL judgement implications flagged.

**Going concern.** Interim directors' report confirms going concern with covenant headroom under base case and severe but plausible downside (−30% revenue on work to be secured, −300bps margin). Leverage below zero; interest cover 11.8×. Principal risks unchanged from FY2025 annual report pages 36–39 (not fully extracted in body files).

RiskTags: cyclical, regulatory, pension, competitive, customer_concentration, other

research_rationale: Filings confirm improving margins, net-cash balance sheet, pension de-risking and record forward work that support the quantitative buy signal, partially offset by revenue decline, HS2/programme uncertainty and sector cost-overrun noise requiring patience on the FY2027 step-change narrative.

open_questions: FY2022–FY2025 Yahoo annuals show revenue falling from ~£1.42bn to ~£1.05bn while operating profit and FCF rose — is the screen’s quality/GARP pass a durable higher-margin mix shift (consultancy/services vs construction) or a shrinking, de-risked book that eventually caps growth?

H1 2026 RNS/call headlines claim an “inflection point” and a ~£7bn forward work position; how much of that is legally contracted vs preferred-bidder/framework places (e.g. the £700m TfL win is a framework seat), and what is the conversion/timing risk into FY2026–28 revenue?

Do the FY2025 Companies House accounts and H1 2026 interim disclose contract-risk items typical of a UK contractor — onerous-contract provisions, claims/unagreed variations, retentions, performance bonds, joint-venture recourse, and fixed-price vs cost-reimbursable mix — that the cheapness/quality models ignore?

How free is the ~£189m cash? Restricted cash was ~£26m at FY2025, current ratio is 1.44 (fails Graham Defensive), FY2025 working-capital outflow was ~£9.5m, and TTM cash-flow is suppressed because quarterly cashflow is empty — what do statutory cash notes and H1 cash say about bonds, escrow, and cash conversion?
Defined-benefit pension surplus is ~£60m on the FY2025 Yahoo balance sheet — is that surplus recoverable, and what deficit/contribution risk appears if discount rates fall?

Ongoing 2026 “Transaction in Own Shares” plus ~£12m FY2025 buybacks shrink the share count (Piotroski “no dilution” passed) while the signal is only 1 week old — how much of the 15.5x P/E, FCF-yield, and EPS-growth (~22%) scores is buyback-inflated rather than operating?

Screen FCF is tagged currency=USD on a GBP LSE name (canonical £48.5m filing-aligned vs screen TTM £49.6m) — do filing-body sterling figures confirm the multiples, or is there a unit/FX integrity error in the strong-buy score?

Cyclical/public-capex overlay is off despite water AMP, transport/HS2 overrun news, energy/nuclear, and UK Spending Review dependence — what do FY2025/H1 filings say about customer concentration (National Highways, TfL, water majors) and FY2026 guidance vs the May 2026 AGM trading update?
Post-H1 press cites analyst value ~£2.57 vs the screen’s core limit £2.15 / tactical £1.89 — has the H1 print already rerated the name so the “new strong buy” is stale relative to live price?
Kalkine “UK Defence Stocks: COST…” vs Costain’s civil-infrastructure identity — is there a real nuclear/defence mix change in the filings, or ticker-collision noise that must not inform the memo?

meta_reflection.observation: Evidence ladder correctly ranks filing bodies first, and COST.L has 8 annual + 1 interim + 1 trading-update bodies. But investegate_resolved ingested non-issuer RNSs via the token “cost” (Atlantic Lithium, Cadence Minerals, Anglo Asian Mining, Capita, Pennon, United Utilities). Workers reading filings_index by headline will contaminate a Costain memo unless issuer ticker/company number is a hard filter.

News query `"Costain Group PLC" OR COST stock UK` floods the manifest with Costco (COST), Tesco/BT/Vodafone/ISA “cost” pieces. Alternate_news is a listed thin/missing step, so there is no clean second news channel. Digest prompts must require issuer=Costain and discard substring hits; otherwise qualitative tone will be garbage.

Ladder + four task types + 5-task cap is adequate for annual/interim/news/screen/gaps, but drops the 2026-05-14 AGM trading update and the June–July contract RNSs (TfL, West Winch, United Utilities) that sit in filings_index as period=other. For a contractor, those are first-class evidence, not optional colour.

conviction_score 0.442, weeks_at_signal=1, stability=new, timing=neutral — the screen already knows this is a fresh print. Overlays are all false, including cyclical_exposure, cash_conversion, and interim_quality, on a UK infrastructure contractor just after H1. Sector overlays are not firing where they should.

financials_annual.json is Yahoo-shaped (years 2021–2025; quarterly_income/quarterly_cashflow empty; ttm_cashflow_suppressed). screening_snapshot.fcf.currency is USD. There is no schema field for order book, secured vs preferred, or framework conversion — the exact quantities a Costain verify-before-trade memo needs. NCAV is flagged missing, which is expected for this model, not a COST.L-specific hole.

Allowed types (summarize_filing_body, digest_news_manifest, screen_context, gap_inventory) cannot express “summarize trading_update” or “cluster contract-win RNSs” without overloading an annual/interim focus string. Director cannot assign IR-metric or quarterly-cashflow reads because those sources are thin/absent — gap_inventory is the right escape hatch, but it only inventories, it does not fill.

Ladder order is sound (filings_bodies → filings_index → yahoo_financials → yahoo_quarterly_cashflow → news → alternate_news → screening → screen_run → ir_metrics → macro). Thin steps match the inventory: no ir_presentation_metrics file, no alternate_news file, empty Yahoo quarterlies. IR allowlist in filings_index.note did not fire despite an Investor Meet Company RNS — ingest gap, not ladder-order gap.

Director-only catalog pass can form ticker-specific questions (revenue/profit divergence, framework vs backlog, cash restrictedness, pension, buybacks, FX tag) without drafting the memo. Blind spot: body_path in filings_index points at docs/data/research/COST.L/... not the trial snapshot tree; workers need an explicit remap rule or they will miss bodies.

Piotroski 8/9 fails only asset turnover — consistent with falling revenue — yet the name is still strong_buy across cheapness/quality/dividend/GARP/risk. Scoring lacks a contractor-specific WIP/claims/cash-conversion brake, so the director–worker loop is being asked to qualitatively veto a mechanically clean screen.
